institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That they had courses within my academic interest

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only a 7 as I did not like the structure of the host university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were welcoming days with presentations on what and how to do things, opportunities to have a friends~buddy, and a lot of social events

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Through my degree I already had connections which luckily made it easy to find housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there a lot of shared flats available and they can be found on an app called "WG gesucht".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Firstly before arriving we had to come up with a list of courses we wanted to take. Then after arrival when we recieved the login information and could actually acces the platform and sign up for courses and see additional information very little of what we had planned ahead and spent time on before leaving could be used as the time tables etc. did not work out. So a lot of time, at least 10-20 hours, was spent during the first weeks to search for courses and making them align so that attending the classes was possible. Sadly, many of us ending up taking courses out of practicalities and not academic interest. Furthermore, a lot of paperwork has been required of us throughout the stay and often it is the same documents that have to be sent to different people or uploaded on different platforms resulting in a lot of stress as you constantly felt like you had forgotten something which could be of importance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
They had a lot of presentations in the beginning on how to navigate and then an email and office where you could go (however long responds time on email). 
For each degree a tutor/older students was hired to help out. This was very nice. They would arrange social events, remind us of deadlines, and answer questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Once I had found courses that fitted each other time wise I was lucky to get in on all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That one need to prepare for a lot of paperwork but that it is doable with a good cup of coffee and steady nerves.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The courses were too small, 1-3 ECTS, so I feel like the learning outcome is not so high as it could have been. 
The structure of the academic year was also a bit confusing compared to what I am used to as courses, exams etc. could overlap and time and dates change from one day to another.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
For some courses the academic level was very high and for others low. But in general the small courses didn't offer you a lot of time to actually get to know the taught stuff so much information was lost unfortunately. 
The courses with a high level often expected you to have previous knowledge even though it wasn't necessarily stated on the course description.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very based on classical lectures. Very little interaction between students and professors. And also very little interaction between students. And when there was interaction one could clearly tell that they did not have a lot of experinece with it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
On the second semester I was doing my thesis so: 
- thesis 
- thesis seminar

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The two "Specific methods in soil analysis" were very good as you were introduced to a lot of methods in the lab and you had a change to have hands on experience with all of them. The class was very small and many professord/helpers were there to guide you and answer questions.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The semester ticket for travelling within Vienna is cheap ~ 100 DKK per month. But traveling outside the city is more expensive why buying a Klimaticket makes sense even though it is around 6,000.00 DKK but then you have unlimited transportation within all of Austria. And it is possible to get money back if you can prove that you move out of the country.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more or less the same, a bit cheaper.  However, eating and drinking out is a lot cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit tricky finding English speaking clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All three

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sport as it brings a lot of different people together.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
To visit all the museums. 
Travel outside the city- only a two hours train ride gives you beautiful mountains. 
To have wine on the wine yards just outside the city (Kahlenberg).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very friendly once meeting them. But you have to make an effort.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That people seem a bit grumpy but actually they are not (necessarily at least;) )

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very helpfull wherever you would go even though not all speak English. But they are happy to help in German.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be prepared but not scared of paperwork
2) Enjoy your time and trust that things work out 
3) Don't postpone the things you want to experience

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the Austrian students for advice! The structure is chaotic so follow their way around it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience living in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding your way and adjust to a different University structure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
